source_version: Theory of Computing15(2019),Article12; final publisher source October29,2019, includes corrected proof of Theorem3.1
title: Characterization of locally decodable codes by smooth outlaw distributions

standard_prerequisites.name: Boolean Fourier analysis, Rademacher symmetrization and coding theory
standard_prerequisites.statement: Original smoothness/outlaw/LDC definitions and complete local conversion and VC extraction retained.
standard_prerequisites.use: No collector repair of earlier version: uses final corrected author source directly. No claim that candidate incidence/hypergraph outlaws have been resolved.

core_obligations: The authors convert smooth Boolean-function distributions with large uniform empirical deviation into average-case smooth codes by symmetrization, then use a fat-shattering/VC construction to recover true locally decodable codes. The reverse direction builds smooth low-degree decoding polynomials. Both complete conversions and the corrected final-version proof of the distribution-to-average-code theorem are retained as one characterization.
